messages.subject: Multivariate analysis
parts:
Hi Karl,

I need some help implementing a multivariate approach to my analysis. I want to condition a scan for body fat gain on several different sub-phenotypes (things like, liver triglycerides for each animal, HbA1c.. etc) and look for changes in the LOD score for body fat gain. I was thinking I would just generate a phenotype covariate file similar to the covariate file containing sex/cross info but I see now that the example phenocovar file is not necessarily built for data from individuals but the phenotypes themselves.

I've tried just adding the phenotypes as covariates in the file with sex/cross info and I don't see any changes. Not sure if this is a real result or just error on my part. I've tried with two things that ~should~ be casually related-- total and HDL cholesterol QTLs. Maybe I need to list the phenotype as a covariate in the YAML? 

Thanks for your time!
Anna

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl2-disc] Multivariate analysis
parts:
phenotype covariates are different from what you want. They are things that describe the set of phenotypes. Like if the phenotypes are gene expression traits, the phenotype covariates might include things like gene identifier, chromosome, and position, and maybe like tissue.

Include covariates in scan1() with the addcovar argument. You could pull out columns from the phenotype or covariate data in your cross2 object, or you could load them separately. Nothing is done automatically.

karl
